The keeper met Mara at the foot of the lighthouse, a lamp in one hand. He looked at Mara's brown eyes for a long time before he spoke.

"You came back," he said quietly.

She felt the cold wind on her face. The lamp swung in his hand. The lamp threw their shadows up the wall. She saw the lamp flicker and die.

The door was opened by the keeper, and the smell of old oil rolled out to meet them. Two hundred steps wound up into the dark.

"The big tides only come at the half moon," the keeper said. "That is when the bay gives back what it took."

At the top, Mara climbed onto the rail and dove into the deep water without a second thought, swimming out to the black rocks where her father's boat had broken.
